# Ground-truth backtest (generated by ground_fit.py)

**Ground truth:** ARPANSA one-minute UV Index from calibrated radiometers, averaged to hours. 8 stations (Alice Springs, Brisbane, Darwin, Kingston, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney, Townsville), four 3-week windows in 2024 (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct), 5344 daytime hours, 599 station-days.

**Model side:** the app's own `readUV`, fed with what the app would have fetched for the privacy cell (Open-Meteo historical forecast, satellite GHI on the 5x5 lattice, CAMS via the air-quality API). Fitted rows are **leave-one-station-out**.

## Scorecard

Daily dose = sum of hourly UVI over the station-day. *Under-days* = share of days where predicted dose < 80% of measured: the dangerous direction for a burn app.

| source | hourly RMSE (UVI) | hourly bias | r | daily dose error | daily dose bias | under-days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-Meteo forecast UVI (app default, no satellite) | 1.67 | +6.6% | 0.838 | 24.8% | +14.2% | 9.0% |
| Physics: Allaart x layered CMF (current fit) | 1.30 | -5.0% | 0.905 | 19.9% | -0.4% | 20.2% |
| CAMS all-sky UVI x s (LOCO) | 1.17 | -5.8% | 0.924 | 12.3% | -4.9% | 13.0% |
| NEW fallback: s x CAMS clear x layered CMF refit on ground (LOCO) | 1.18 | -1.1% | 0.920 | 14.3% | +3.0% | 4.2% |
| NEW satellite: s x CAMS clear x k_c^p, no delay (LOCO) | 0.68 | -0.3% | 0.974 | 5.8% | -0.7% | 0.5% |
| App as shipped (TS readUV), no satellite (in-sample) | 1.16 | -1.2% | 0.923 | 14.1% | +2.9% | 3.7% |
| App as shipped, satellite, no delay (in-sample) | 0.65 | -0.1% | 0.976 | 5.6% | -0.5% | 0.3% |
| App as shipped, satellite 1 h late (in-sample) | 0.97 | -0.1% | 0.946 | 8.3% | +1.4% | 0.5% |
| App as shipped, satellite 2 h late (in-sample) | 1.06 | -0.3% | 0.936 | 10.0% | +2.2% | 0.5% |

## Live: what the app knows in real time

The rows above give the satellite every slot. Live, the app only has slots that have *arrived*: Open-Meteo serves Himawari ~55–60 min behind real time (measured Nov 2026). ground.ts samples the app every 10 min through each ground hour with only the data available at that instant, then persists the last value with weight e^(−lag/τ) and blends to the no-satellite chain.

Rule: lowest daily dose error among native-data variants at 60-min latency with under-days <= 0.5%. Picked **native_w10_tau4** (window 10 min, τ = 4 h).

| variant | daily dose error | daily dose bias | under-days | hourly RMSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no satellite | 14.1% | +2.9% | 3.7% | 1.16 |
| hourly data, τ 2 h (before step 4) | 9.5% | +0.9% | 0.2% | 0.98 |
| hourly data, τ 4 h | 8.4% | +0.5% | 0.7% | 0.98 |
| native, 10-min window, τ 1 h | 10.5% | +1.0% | 1.0% | 0.95 |
| native, 10-min window, τ 2 h | 8.3% | +0.2% | 0.3% | 0.86 |
| native, 10-min window, τ 4 h | 7.1% | -0.3% | 0.3% | 0.84 |
| native, 10-min window, τ 8 h | 6.7% | -0.7% | 1.0% | 0.85 |
| native, 30-min window, τ 4 h | 7.3% | -0.2% | 0.5% | 0.87 |
| native, 60-min window, τ 4 h | 7.6% | -0.1% | 1.0% | 0.91 |
| native, τ 4 h, if latency were 30 min | 6.3% | -0.8% | 0.5% | 0.74 |
| native, τ 4 h, if latency were 90 min | 8.4% | +0.3% | 0.8% | 0.95 |
| native, all data arrived (after-the-fact) | 5.8% | -1.5% | 0.3% | 0.66 |

Longer τ keeps lowering error slightly but raises under-days (τ 12 h: 6.7% / 1.2%), so the safety cap decides.


## Dose band for time-to-burn (projections from data as of the start)

From each start (every 30 min), predicted dose over the next H hours with only data available then, vs measured. Band = 10th–90th percentile of measured/predicted, burn-relevant windows (mean predicted UVI >= 1.0). The app multiplies the whole dose by `hi` for the cautious time and alerts, and by `lo` for the optimistic time.

| source | 0.5 h | 1 h | 2 h | 4 h | 8 h | LOCO inside band | LOCO above band (worst station) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sat | 0.70–1.24 | 0.72–1.23 | 0.75–1.22 | 0.80–1.22 | 0.83–1.21 | 79% | 11% (Sydney 20%) |
| nwp | 0.64–1.29 | 0.67–1.28 | 0.71–1.25 | 0.77–1.24 | 0.81–1.23 | 79% | 10% (Townsville 25%) |
| legacy | 0.41–1.27 | 0.43–1.26 | 0.48–1.26 | 0.55–1.24 | 0.60–1.21 | 79% | 10% (Alice Springs 26%) |
| physics | 0.67–1.40 | 0.70–1.39 | 0.72–1.37 | 0.74–1.34 | 0.76–1.33 | 79% | 10% (Townsville 32%) |

Nominal: 80% inside, 10% above. Averaged over held-out stations the band is close to nominal, but at single stations measured dose lands above it up to the worst-station figure shown. Treat the cautious time as "plan for this", not a worst case.


## Fitted parameters (all stations)

- CAMS clear-sky scale s = **0.880** (CAMS clear-sky reads 14% high)
- Satellite exponent p = **0.876** with k_c cap 1.0 (shipped guess was 0.6, cap 1.2). Overcast k_c = 0.3 gives CMF 0.35.
- Layered CMF on ground: low: a=0.225, b=0.74 | mid: a=0.250, b=0.76 | high: a=0.125, b=2.06 (full overcast CMF 0.40)

## Clear-sky curves vs ground (satellite-clear hours, median ground / model)

| SZA band | n | Allaart (300 DU) | Open-Meteo clear | s x CAMS clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (0, 20] | 229 | 1.013 | 1.222 | 1.022 |
| (20, 35] | 479 | 0.997 | 1.087 | 1.032 |
| (35, 50] | 773 | 1.130 | 0.943 | 1.015 |
| (50, 65] | 863 | 1.142 | 0.702 | 0.975 |
| (65, 85] | 156 | 1.159 | 0.547 | 0.942 |

| month (2024) | Allaart (300 DU) | s x CAMS clear |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | 1.101 | 1.022 |
| 04 | 1.198 | 1.014 |
| 07 | 1.181 | 1.007 |
| 10 | 0.933 | 1.009 |

Allaart's error follows the Southern Hemisphere ozone cycle (October high ozone → reads high; April low → reads low), because the app uses a fixed 300 DU. CAMS carries forecast ozone and aerosol, so its ratio is flat across months and needs only one scale factor.

## Limitations (say these out loud)

- All stations are in Australia: low aerosol and Southern Hemisphere ozone. The CAMS scale and satellite exponent are fitted there; no US or European ground station is in the fit yet.
- Broadband radiometers have their own ~5% calibration uncertainty.
- The historical forecast is stitched from short-lead runs, which flatters the forecast compared with a 2-day-ahead plan.
- Hourly means hide minute-scale broken-cloud spikes.
